descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can match a picture to a character or event from a story I have heard or read. In informational texts, I can point to a named detail or picture that relates to the topic.

I can respond to peers’ communications to them by looking in the direction of the speaker and nodding.
I can use a single message voice output device to say, “Who has more to say?” during a group discussion.
I can use a sequenced message device to participate in an interaction about an activity in the classroom using social scripts.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Answer specific questions related to information in a discussion.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can ask and answer questions about information presented by others.
I can respond to teacher’s question about peer’s story, “Are most tomatoes bigger than a basketball?” with “No!” when teacher says, “What do you want to know?,” the student says, “Is that real?”
I can after a peer completes a class presentation about a state hero, ask, “What happened to him?” The peer says, “He won the war. Do you remember the name of the war?,” students answer.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can ask and answer questions about the topic.
I can While looking at a picture of the big tomato a classmate is sharing, ask, “Can you eat it?”
I can While looking at a picture from a peer’s class presentation about a state hero such as a fireman, point to the picture of the hose when asked, “Where is the hero’s tools/equipment?”
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, answer questions about the topic.
I can While looking at a picture of the big tomato a classmate is sharing, the teacher asks, “What do you do with a tomato?,” point to eat as a correct answer.
I can While looking at a picture from a peer’s class presentation about a state hero such as a fireman, point to the picture of the hose when asked, “Where is the hero’s tools/equipment?”

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify the key ideas in a discussion.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the key ideas of the discussion.
I can Use a voice output system to say, “big, tomato, farm market.”
I can Point to an illustration in a science textbook to identify the topic of a discussion.
I can Say, “the characters” when asked, “What part of the book are we talking about?”
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify one idea presented in the discussion.
I can Point to or eye gaze to a picture of the big tomato from an array of pictures of various vegetables.
I can Use multiple message voice output device to select a symbol that represents one idea in a discussion.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify the topic of the discussion.
I can Select from two illustrations showing topics of the discussion (e.g., when the teacher says, “We are talking about Amy’s trip to the farmer’s market. What did she say she saw?” Then, holds up and labels two pictures, the student eye gazes to the picture of the tomato.).
I can During a small group literature circle discussion, point to the appropriate book when a peer holds up two books and asks, “What book are we talking about?”

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Ask and answer questions about details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the main idea of a text presented through diverse media.
I can after listening to a peer read a text that is projected on an interactive whiteboard, identify the main idea from choices presented at the end of the book.
I can after seeing a video clip of a pumpkin growing in slow motion, state main idea, “pumpkins grow in stages.”
I can after seeing a video clip of a pumpkin growing in slow motion, use a multiple message voice output device to say, “pumpkins grow.”
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify details from a text presented through diverse media.
I can after seeing a video clip of a pumpkin growing in slow motion, identify details from the video (e.g., seed, stem, leaves, pumpkin).
I can after listening to a peer read a text that is projected on an interactive whiteboard, sort pictures into boxes of those that are details from the story and those that are not.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify the topic of a text presented through diverse media.
I can after watching with focused attention to a video clip of showing a pumpkin growing in slow motion, point to a picture of a pumpkin from an array of choices when asked, “What was that movie about?”
I can after listening to a peer read a text that is projected on an interactive whiteboard, point to a picture from an array that represents the topic of the book.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify a point that the speaker makes.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify a point that the speaker makes.
I can Restate in a word or two a point the speaker makes on the topic (e.g., states a reason Fern used to convince her father to keep Wilbur).
I can after listening to a peer present to the class, identify two things the peer said from a list presented with partner-assisted scanning (e.g., The peer reads each item in the list and the student says, “yes” or “no” to indicate if the item was part of what peer said in presentation).
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, repeat one point a speaker makes.
I can Repeat a phrase the speaker has said when asked (e.g., The student points to a picture of one of the messages Charlotte puts on her web, such as “some pig”, when asked, “What did Charlotte say that saved Wilbur?”).
I can Select a pre-stored message from an array of choices to repeat a point the speaker makes.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize speaker.
I can Establish eye gaze with speaker.
I can Face toward the speaker.
I can Nod or otherwise acknowledge the speaker.
I can Point to speaker when asked, “Who is speaking?”

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Clearly retell a story, poem, or personal experience or recount a topic with supporting details.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can tell a story about a personal experience with supporting details.
I can Using a sign, tell about the puppy arriving at home, including details about the first encounter with the puppy (e.g., “We got a puppy at the store. He rode next to me in the car. He jumped on me. We played a lot.”).
I can Before writing, tell the teacher what they are going to write about (e.g., The student says, “I went to the party. Grandma Red Hat party. Aunt Stephanie and I have a party. I got a new dress.”).
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can recount a personal experience including details.
I can use a multiple message voice output device, and select three symbols to show how he or she made the cookies (e.g., mix, cook, oven).
I can use a multiple voice output communication device to report on weekend activities during a morning meeting (e.g., The student says, “Shopping with mom. Shoes, DVD, lunch.”).
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify a picture, object, or other artifact from a personal experience.
I can given an array of pictures, point to the appropriate picture when the teacher says, “You got a new puppy? Show me the picture of your new puppy.”
I can given a display of class art projects, identify own project.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Add audio recordings or visuals to a presentation about a personally relevant topic.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can add audio recordings or visuals to a presentation about a personally relevant topic.
I can select pictures from a family vacation, label the pictures (e.g., people’s names and places) and sequence them for a presentation.
I can select objects from a collection (e.g., toys, rocks, videos) and select words from a multiple message communication device to go with each object to use in a presentation.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can select pictures, objects, or artifacts or label pictures, objects, or artifacts to contribute to a simple presentation about a personally relevant topic.
I can work with a small group, create a presentation about a class activity (e.g., Creating a presentation about a class trip to a diamond mine, the student selects a sieve, trowel, and diamond chip for the group to include in the presentation.).
I can work with other family members, select pictures of members of the family to show during a presentation about family.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can select a picture, object, or artifact from an array of options to add to a class-created presentation about a personally relevant topic.
I can select favorite picture of the new puppy to add to the presentation Our Pets created by the class.
I can select a favorite food item from an array to add to a class presentation Our Favorite Things created by the class.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use drawings, dictation, or writing to compose different types of writing for different purposes with help from my teacher.
I can The student participates in a writing workshop where they choose to write a story about a magical creature (low-stakes) and later drafts an informational paragraph about their favorite animal with facts and details (high-stakes). They may use any combination of drawing, dictation, or writing to complete these tasks.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use drawings and dictation to tell a story or share information with help from my teacher.
I can The student draws a picture of their family and dictates a sentence about each family member to the teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use drawings to express my ideas and interests.
I can The student draws a picture of a playground and uses gestures or single words to share details about their drawing.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, use writing, dictation and/or drawing to compose: a. Opinion pieces in which they state an opinion about a topic or text and include some reasons to support that opinion.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use drawing, dictation, or writing to create opinion pieces, informational texts, and narratives with help from my teacher. I can share my opinions with reasons, teach others about a topic, and tell stories with a beginning, middle, and end.
I can The student dictates an opinion piece about their favorite season, providing reasons why they like it. They draw and label a diagram of a plant for an informational report. They write a short story about a time they went to the zoo, including details about the animals they saw.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use drawing and dictation to share my opinions, give information about a topic, and tell simple stories with help from my teacher.
I can The student draws a picture of their favorite food and dictates a sentence about why they like it. They work with a partner to create a poster with pictures and labels about different types of transportation. They retell a familiar story using pictures and simple sentences.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use drawings and some words to express my opinions, share information, and tell a story.
I can The student draws a picture of themselves playing with a friend and dictates a sentence about what they are doing. They draw a picture of a recent event and label objects in the picture.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Informative/Explanatory text in which they introduce a topic and provide some facts, details, and/or multimedia content about a predetermined or self chosen topic.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write or say facts about a topic and give some details to explain it.
I can use pictures, words, or videos to share information about a topic.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write or say one fact about a topic and include a detail with help.
I can use a picture or word to give some information about a topic with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can point to or say a word or picture about a topic I know with support.
I can use pictures, words, or objects to show what I know about a topic with help.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Convey events, real or imagined and narrate a single event or several loosely linked events. Include some details regarding what happened and tell about the events in the order in which they occurred.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write or tell about something that happened, including details and the order of events.
I can share a story, real or made up, and explain what happened in order.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can say or write about one event and tell what happened with help.
I can share a story with some details about what happened with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use pictures or words to show one event that happened with support.
I can tell or show one part of a story in order with help.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that uses familiar words, transitions to link and build connections, temporal words to signal event order, and a beginning, middle, and end.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use drawing, dictation, or writing to create a story with a beginning, middle, and end. I can use words that tell the order of events and words that connect my ideas.
I can The student writes and illustrates a story about a lost puppy. They use words like "first," "then," and "finally" to show the order of events. They also use connecting words like "and" and "but" to make their writing smoother.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use drawing and dictation to tell a story with a beginning, middle, and end. I can use some words that tell the order of events.
I can The student draws a series of pictures about their trip to the beach. With teacher support, they dictate sentences about each picture, using words like "first" and "then" to show the order of their activities.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use drawings and some words to tell a story. I can put events in order.
I can The student draws three pictures to show what they did during their morning routine. They can point to each picture and use a word or two to describe what happened first, next, and last.

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, produce writing that is appropriate for an explicitly stated task or purpose, and expresses more than one idea.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write for different purposes when my teacher tells me what the purpose is. I can share more than one idea in my writing.
I can when asked to write a letter to a friend about their favorite game, the student includes multiple reasons why they enjoy the game and details about how it is played.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can writ]e for different purposes when my teacher tells me what the purpose is. I can share one or two ideas in my writing.
I can when asked to write a description of a picture, the student writes one or two sentences about what they see.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write a few words or draw a picture to respond to a prompt.
I can when asked to write about their favorite animal, the student draws a picture of the animal and writes its name.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support from adults and peers, plan before writing and produce writing focused on the planned topic, and revise their own writing, dictation, or pictures.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can plan what I am going to write or draw before I start. I can use my plan to help me stay on topic. I can make changes to my writing or drawings to make them better.
I can Before writing a story about a superhero, the student brainstorms ideas with a partner, creates a simple story map, and uses it to guide their writing. after writing, they review their work with a teacher, adding details and fixing errors.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use a planning strategy, like talking to my teacher or looking at pictures, before I write or draw. I can make some changes to my work when my teacher reminds me.
I can Before writing about their favorite animal, the student looks at pictures of animals with the teacher and talks about what they find interesting. after dictation, they listen to the teacher reread their sentences and help fix any mistakes.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can talk about my ideas with my teacher before I draw a picture. I can add more details to my drawings when my teacher helps me.
I can Before drawing a picture about their family, the student tells their teacher who they want to include in the picture. after finishing the drawing, they add details like hair color and clothing with prompting from the teacher.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support from adults, use digital tools, including the Internet, to produce writing while interacting and collaborating with others. Learn to produce writing through printing and/or typing.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use a computer or tablet to write with help from my teacher. I can use the internet to find information for my writing. I can share my writing with others and work together on writing projects.
I can The student uses a graphic organizer on a tablet to plan a report about an animal. They search for pictures and information on a kid-friendly website with teacher guidance. They practice typing sentences for their report and share their writing with a partner for feedback.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use a computer or tablet to write with help from my teacher. I can practice typing or printing my ideas.
I can The student uses a talking word processor to write a sentence about a picture. They practice typing their name and simple words on the keyboard with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use a computer or tablet to draw and write letters or my name.
I can The student uses a drawing app to create a picture and explores the keyboard to type letters or their name with assistance.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, identify information about two or more aspects of a shared or independent inquiry topic.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can learn about a topic from different sources with help from my teacher. I can share at least two different things that I learned about the topic.
I can During a class study of weather, the student explores books and websites (with teacher guidance) to learn about different types of clouds and how rain forms. They can share details about both aspects of the topic.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can learn about a topic from pictures and books with help from my teacher. I can answer questions about what I learned.
I can when learning about the life cycle of a butterfly, the student looks at pictures and listens to a book read aloud. They can answer questions about a butterfly's different stages of development.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can ask questions about a topic I want to learn more about. I can identify a few key details about a topic from pictures.
I can when shown pictures of different ocean animals, the student asks, "What do they eat?" after listening to a simple book about whales, they can point to a picture of a whale and say, "It lives in the ocean."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Recall and sort information from personal experiences or a topic into given categories and write or draw about each one.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can organize my ideas into different groups and then write or draw about each group.
I can after brainstorming a list of things they do in different seasons, the student sorts their ideas into categories (fall, winter, spring, summer). They then choose one season and write a paragraph describing their favorite activities during that time of year.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can sort pictures or objects into groups and then say a sentence about each group.
I can given a collection of toy animals from different habitats (farm, ocean, jungle), the student sorts them into the correct groups. They can then describe each group by saying a simple sentence, such as, "These animals live on a farm."
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can match objects or pictures to categories.
I can when shown pictures of different foods and given categories like "fruits" and "vegetables," the student can match the pictures to the correct groups.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support from adults, recall key details from literary or informational texts to support reflection or inquiry questions based on a reading of a literary or informational text.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can remember important details from a story or informational text. I can use those details to answer questions and share my thinking about the text.
I can after listening to a story about a child who overcomes a fear, the student can recall details about how the character felt and what they did to face their fear. They can use these details to answer questions like, "How did the character change in the story?"
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can remember some details from a story or informational text. I can answer simple questions about the text with help from my teacher.
I can after listening to a nonfiction text about different types of birds, the student can recall one or two details about a specific bird. With prompting from the teacher, they can answer a question like, "What does a woodpecker eat?"
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can answer yes/no or pointing questions about a story or informational text.
I can after listening to a story about a trip to the zoo, the student can point to the animal when asked, "Did they see a lion?"

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Use language to achieve desired meaning when communicating. a. Notice that standardized English is only one dialect of many.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I understand that people speak in different dialects, and I can identify some of those differences.
Ex: A student can listen to recordings of speakers from different regions of the United States and identify unique words or pronunciations used in each region.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
Adapts language choices in familiar situations to enhance communication.
Example: A student asks a friend, "Can I borrow a pencil?" but asks the teacher, "Excuse me, may I please borrow a pencil?" recognizing the need for a more formal request in the latter situation.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
Uses concrete language and non-verbal cues to convey basic meaning.
Example: A student acts out the word "tired" by pretending to sleep or rubbing their eyes.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Notice the differences in language between familiar and unfamiliar contexts.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify differences in how people speak in different situations.
Ex: After listening to recordings of people talking at home and at work, a student can point out words or phrases that are used in one setting but not the other.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can change how I talk depending on who I am talking to.
Ex: A student can practice using a louder voice when speaking to a group than when talking to a friend.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can follow directions that use different words to mean the same thing.
Ex: A student can respond appropriately to both "come here" and "walk over here," demonstrating understanding of synonyms in context.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Notice the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify when characters in stories use different ways of speaking.
Ex: After listening to a story with characters who speak in different dialects, a student can point to each character when their specific way of speaking is played back.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can tell that the way characters speak in stories can be different from how I speak.
Ex: When a teacher reads a story aloud using a distinct accent or dialect, a student can identify that the way the characters are speaking sounds different.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can tell that the way characters speak in stories can be different from how I speak with support.
Ex: A student can sit attentively and listen to a story read aloud to be able to respond to simple questions.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Expand sentences for meaning, interest, and style.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can add details to my sentences to make them more interesting and give more information.
Ex: When shown a picture of a cat sleeping in a basket, a student can expand the sentence "The cat is sleeping" to "The fluffy cat is sleeping soundly in the blue basket."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can make my sentences longer by adding words.
Ex: When prompted to describe a picture, a student can add words to "The boy runs" to make it "The boy runs fast."
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can put words together to make simple sentences.
Ex: When shown a picture, a student can construct a basic sentence like "The dog barks."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. a. Use frequently occurring root words (e.g., talk) and the words that result when word endings are added (e.g., talked, talking, talks).

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the root word in different words and understand that adding endings to a root word can change how we use it in a sentence.
Ex: A student understands that "walk," "walked," "walking," and "walker" are all related to the same root word and can use them correctly in sentences.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can recognize the same root word in different words when these words sound similar.
Ex: When presented with the words "help" and "helper," the student can identify that they share a common root word.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can match pictures to words that share the same root word.
Ex: When shown pictures of a child drawing a picture and a colorful drawing hanging on the refrigerator, the student can match them to the words "draw" and "drawing."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Demonstrate understanding of word relationship and use. a. Determine the literal meaning of words and phrases in context.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can figure out the everyday meaning of words and phrases when I read them in a story or text. I can also understand and use words that have similar meanings. I can identify and use different words to describe how I am feeling.
Ex: A student understands that "happy," "joyful," and "cheerful" have similar meanings and can use them interchangeably. They can also use words like "upset," "frustrated," and "angry" to express different levels of negative emotions.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can understand what words and phrases mean when I read them in a story or text. I can tell when words have almost the same meaning.
Ex: When asked, "What's another word for 'big'?" the student can provide "large" or "huge."
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can understand the simple meaning of words I see often.
Ex: The student understands the meaning of common words like "happy," "sad," "big," "small," "eat," and "play."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Not applicable
source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Demonstrate understanding of words that have similar meanings

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can explain how two words mean almost the same thing, like “happy” and “joyful.”
I can use words that are similar in meaning in my sentences to describe things.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can point to or say two words that have similar meanings, like “big” and “large,” with help.
I can recognize when two words mean the same thing with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can listen to two words that have similar meanings and point to a picture that shows what they mean with support.
I can recognize one word that means the same as another word with help.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify words that describe an increasing number of personal emotional states.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use words like “excited,” “worried,” or “proud” to describe my feelings in different situations.
I can name and describe different emotions I feel throughout the day.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can say or point to words like “happy” or “scared” to describe how I feel with help.
I can match a word to how I feel when someone asks me with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can respond to words like “sad” or “angry” when someone asks how I feel with support.
I can point to a picture or say a word that shows my feelings with help.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Use words acquired through conversations, being read to, and during shared reading activities including domain- specific words. a. Identify conjunctions

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use new formal/academic words that I learn from talking with others, listening to stories, and reading together with my class. I can use these words, even special words related to what we are learning about, in my own writing and speaking. I can also identify conjunctions (words like "and," "but," "or") in sentences.
Ex: After a lesson on weather, a student uses words like "precipitation," "temperature," and "forecast" in a conversation about the day's weather.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can understand and use new words that I hear when people talk and when I am read to. I can sometimes use these words to talk about what I am learning in different subjects.
Ex: A student, after listening to a story about a farm, correctly uses words like "tractor" and "harvest" in a sentence.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can understand and use new basic words that I hear often in different places.
Ex: A student learns and uses a new word like "vehicle" after it is introduced and reinforced in various contexts (e.g., books, classroom discussions, real-life observations).

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Demonstrate standardized English grammar and usage when communicating. a. Use frequently occurring conjunctions: and, but, or, for, because.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
With support, I can sometimes use the correct grammar and word forms when I am talking and writing. I can use conjunctions like "and," "but," "or," "for," and "because" to connect my ideas. I can also use the past tense of common irregular verbs, like "went," "sat," "ate," and "told," correctly.
Ex: A student, when recounting a past event, accurately uses verbs like "went" and "saw" instead of "goed" and "seed."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I am learning to use the correct grammar when I am talking and writing. I can use simple conjunctions like "and" and "but" to connect my ideas. I am learning to use the past tense of common verbs.
Ex: A student uses "and" to connect two ideas in a sentence but may need prompting to use other conjunctions like "because" to express a reason.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I am learning to use words to tell you what I am thinking. I am learning to use words like "and" to connect my ideas. I am learning about action words.
Ex: A student, when describing a picture, can use simple sentences like "The boy went to the park" with appropriate verb tense.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregularverbs (e.g., went, sat, ate, told)

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use past tense verbs like “went,” “ate,” or “sat” to talk about something that happened.
I can tell a story using the correct past tense of common verbs, like “told” or “saw.”
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can say or write past tense verbs like “went” or “ate” with help.
I can use past tense verbs when talking about something that happened with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can listen to a sentence about the past and repeat the correct verb, like “sat” or “went,” with support.
I can recognize and use one action that happened in the past with help.

subject: ELA
text: Demonstrate understanding of conventions of standardized English.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I am learning to use the correct spelling, punctuation, and capitalization when I am writing. I can sound out words I don't know using what I know about letters and sounds and spelling patterns to try to spell them correctly.
Ex: A student attempts to spell "community" as "komunitee," demonstrating an understanding of phonetic spelling and common letter combinations.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I am learning to use what I know about letters and sounds to spell words.
Ex: A student, when asked to write "rain," can segment the sounds and write "ran" or "rane," showing progress in applying phonics knowledge.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify different letters of the alphabet. I am learning the sounds that letters make.
Ex: A student can identify the letters in their name and attempt to write some of them, demonstrating early literacy development.

subject: ELA

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Spell untaught word phonetically, drawing on letter-sound relationships and common spelling patterns.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can spell new words by sounding them out, using what I know about letter sounds and spelling patterns.
I can use what I know about letters and sounds to spell words that I haven’t learned yet.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can try to spell words I don’t know by saying the sounds I hear with help.
I can write some letters that match the sounds of a word with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can listen to a word and say or write one of the sounds I hear with support.
I can use pictures or letters to show how a word sounds with help.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify explicit details in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify and recall key details and information directly stated in a text. 
I can answer basic comprehension questions using explicit textual evidence.
Example: "The cat is fluffy, and it's sitting on a mat. The text says the cat purrs loudly because it's happy."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can select words or phrases from the text that provide clues about the meaning, even if the connection isn't fully formed. 
I can use picture and context clues to make simple inferences.
Example: (Teacher asks: "How do we know the cat likes the mat?") Student: "It says 'soft mat' and 'purred loudly.'"
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify words, pictures, or phrases in the text when prompted with simple, direct questions about explicit information.
Example: (Teacher points to the word "cat" in the text) "Can you find this word in the text? What word tells us what the cat is doing?" Student: (points to "sat") "Sat."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify the theme or main idea from a text when it is not explicitly stated. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can dentify some key details in a text and begin to understand the main idea or theme but I need help explaining how the details support it.
 I can identify the main idea of a text with support from the teacher or a partner.
Example: "The book The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe is about four kids who find a magical world inside a wardrobe. There's a mean witch who turns things to stone and a lion named Aslan who is good. I think the main idea is about being brave, but I'm not sure how Aslan coming back to life shows that."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I require extensive support to identify the main idea or theme.
I may be able to identify key characters or events in a story with prompting.
Example: (Teacher points to a picture of Aslan) "Who is this?" ... "Can you say Aslan?"... (Teacher points to a picture of the White Witch) "And who is this?"
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I demonstrate an understanding of the basic elements of a story, such as characters and events, and I can answer simple questions about them with support. 
I may be able to retell a familiar story with prompting, using key words or phrases.
Example: (After listening to the teacher read The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe) Teacher: "Who went to Narnia?" Student: "The children." Teacher: "Yes, and who did they meet in Narnia?" Student: "Aslan... and the witch."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Compare two characters in a familiar story. (RL) Compare two individuals, events or ideas in a text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can compare two characters, individuals, events, or ideas in a simple or short story. 
I can identify clear similarities and differences and provide some basic textual support for their claims. Example: "The tortoise and the hare are different. The hare is fast, but the tortoise is slow. The story says the hare ran quickly and took a nap. The tortoise went slow and steady and won the race."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can make basic connections between two individuals or events/actions in a simple or short story with support from the teacher or a partner. 
I may rely on picture clues and context to identify relationships. 
Example: (Teacher points to a picture of the hare sleeping) "What is the hare doing?" Student: "Sleeping." (Teacher points to a picture of the tortoise crossing the finish line) "Who won the race?" Student: "The tortoise."
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can demonstrate an understanding of who the characters are in a familiar, simple or short story and can answer simple questions about them with support. 
Example: (After listening to the teacher read The Tortoise and the Hare) Teacher: "Who was very fast?" Student: "The hare." Teacher: "And who was very slow?" Student: "The tortoise."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Determine the intended meaning of multimeaning and domain-specific words and phrases. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_at_target: Determines the meaning of some multi-meaning words and domain-specific phrases in a text using context clues. May need support with less familiar terms. Example: "I think 'heavy precipitation' means a lot of rain or snow is happening. The text talked about floods after heavy precipitation, so it must be a lot of water falling."
descriptors.cc_approaching: Identifies domain-specific words and phrases in a text with support from the teacher or visual aids. Can demonstrate understanding of basic meanings with prompting. Example: (Teacher points to the phrase "heavy precipitation" in the text) "Can you find this phrase in the text? What do you think it means?" Student: "Hmm, maybe a lot of rain?"
descriptors.cc_emerging: Identifies familiar words and phrases in a text with support. May need picture clues, repeated readings, or direct guidance to connect words to their meanings. Example: (Teacher points to a picture of heavy rain in the text) "What is this picture showing? Can you find the words in the text that match this picture?" Student (pointing to "heavy precipitation"): "Here!"

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, identify a story element that undergoes change from beginning to end (RL) and determine if a text tells about events, gives directions, or provides information on a topic (RI).

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can with support, identify a basic change in a story element from beginning to end and can sort different types of texts (stories, directions, information).
Example: (Teacher, pointing to the first sentence of the RL text: "How does the caterpillar feel at the beginning?") Student: "Scared." (Teacher, pointing to the last sentence: "How about at the end?") Student: "Not scared anymore."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify the beginning, middle, and end of a short text or story with a clear, sequential structure when given support.
Example: (Teacher points to pictures representing the RL text: caterpillar hiding, cocoon, butterfly flying) "Can you put these pictures in order? What happened first, second, last?"
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with significant support, identify the beginning and end of a very simple story or text.
Example: (Teacher points to the first page of the RL text) "Where does the story start?" (Teacher points to the last page) "Where does the story end?"

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, determine the point of view of a narrator (RL); compare two texts on the same topic (RI).

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can with guidance, identify the point of view in a simple story and can find basic similarities between texts on the same topic.
Example: (Teacher: "Whose eyes are we seeing the story through?") Student: "The puppy's."
Example: (Teacher: "What is the same in both of these penguin paragraphs?") Student: "They both talk about penguins."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can with support, identify who is telling a simple story.
Example: (Teacher points to a picture of the puppy in the story) "Who is telling this story?"
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with significant support and visual cues, recognize that who is telling the story.
Example: (Teacher points to a thought bubble above the puppy's head) "This story is told from inside the puppy's head. We know what the puppy is thinking."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify illustrations, tactual or multimedia elements that add to understanding of a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify specific visual elements in a text and I can explain how those elements help me understand the story better.
Example: "The picture shows Corduroy looking sad because he lost his button."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify visual elements in a text that directly represent what is happening in the story.
Example: (Teacher: "Point to the picture that shows Corduroy looking for his button.")
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with support, identify a specific object or character within an illustration when directed.
Example: (Teacher: "Can you point to Corduroy on this page?")

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify the relationship between a specific point and supporting reasons in a text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify a specific point an author is making and match it to a supporting reason or detail provided in a short text.
Example: (Teacher: "Why does the story say helmets are important?") Student: "Because when Max fell off his bike, his helmet protected his head."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can with support, identify a reason or detail within a short text that the author uses to support a point.
Example: (Teacher points to the sentence, "His helmet cracked, but Max's head was safe!") "What does this sentence tell us about why Max is okay?"
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with significant support, identify a specific detail within a short text when prompted.
Example: (Teacher points to the picture of Max's cracked helmet) "What happened to the helmet in the story?"

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Compare and contrast details gained from two texts and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, or situations. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can compare and contrast specific details from two short stories or texts. I can make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, or personal experiences.
Example: "In both stories, the main characters had to be brave. The boy in the bike story had to keep trying even though he fell down. The animals in the flood story had to work together to escape."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can with support, identify similar information presented in two short stories or texts on the same topic.
Example: (Teacher: "What do both stories tell us about what the characters had to do?") Student: "They both had to be brave."
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with support, identify a basic similarity between two short stories or texts with similar topics.
Example: (Teacher: "What is similar about the characters in these two stories?") Student: "They are both animals."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Use letter-sound knowledge to read words. a. Decode and encode common sight words and single syllable words.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can sound out and read words with two or three syllables. I am learning to use what I know about letters and sounds, along with parts of words, to help me read new words.
Ex: A student encounters the word "watermelon" in a story. They can break it into syllables (wa-ter-mel-on), decode each syllable, and blend them together to read the word.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can sound out and read some words with two syllables. I am learning more about how letters and sounds work together. I am starting to learn about parts of words.
Ex: A student encounters the word "sunshine" in a text. They can break it into its component parts ("sun" and "shine"), decode each syllable, and understand the combined meaning.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can sound out words with two syllables. I am learning the sounds that letters make. I am starting to put sounds together to read words.
Ex: A student is presented with the word "in" on a flashcard and can correctly identify the sounds the letters "i" and "n" make. They can then blend those sounds to read the word.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Read words in text. Read text comprised of familiar words with accuracy and understanding. a. Use features of print to identify or verbalize appropriate expression while reading familiar texts.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read texts that have familiar words. I can read smoothly and with expression. When I come across a word I don't know, I can use what I know about letters and sounds, along with clues from the sentence, to figure it out.
Ex: A student is reading a story about a cat and comes across the word "purring." The student uses their knowledge of letter sounds to decode the word and confirms its meaning by connecting it to the cat's happy feeling in the story.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read some texts that have familiar words. I can use what I know about letters and sounds to help me read words. When I come across a word I don't know, I can use clues from the pictures or the sentences to try and figure it out.
Ex: A student is reading a text about animals on a farm and encounters the word "neigh." They may not be able to decode it independently but can use a picture of a horse to infer the word's meaning.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I am learning to read words in stories and books. I am learning to use the pictures to help me understand the words. I am getting better at sounding out words I don't know.
Ex: A student is reading a simple sentence like "The dog is brown." They can point to each word as they read it and use the picture of the brown dog to confirm the meaning of the word "brown."

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Use letter-sound knowledge and context to confirm or self-correct word recognition when reading.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use the sounds of letters and clues from the story to check if a word is correct when I read.
I can fix a word I read wrong by using what I know about letter sounds and what makes sense in the story.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can sound out a word and use pictures or other words in the story to help me figure out if it is correct with help.
I can try to correct a word I don’t know using the first letter and clues from the story with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can listen to the sounds in a word and use a picture or clue from the story to understand it with support.
I can recognize the first sound of a word and check the picture to help me read with help.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Not Applicable.

descriptors.cc_at_target: Not Applicable.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Engage in collaborative discussions. a. Come to discussion prepared to share information from a source such as a text or personal knowledge.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can participate in discussions and share information from what we have read or from my own experiences.
Ex: After reading a nonfiction text about different cultures, students participate in a class discussion. They are able to share a fact they learned from the text and connect it to their own cultural experiences or prior knowledge.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can prepare for discussions with help.
Ex: Before a small group discussion about a story, the teacher provides students with visual prompts or sentence starters to help them organize their thoughts and prepare to share their ideas.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can share my ideas during a class discussion when I have help and support.
Ex: The teacher provides a student with a visual aid, such as a picture card or a communication board, to help them share their thoughts during a class discussion about a familiar topic.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Listen to others’ ideas before responding, gain attention respectfully, and contribute to the discussion.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can listen to others sometimes during a discussion. I can sometimes remember to raise my hand before speaking.
Ex: A student looks at the speaker and may need a reminder to raise their hand before sharing their thought.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can prepare for discussions with help.
Ex: Before a small group discussion about a story, the teacher provides students with visual prompts or sentence starters to help them organize their thoughts and prepare to share their ideas.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can share my ideas during a class discussion when I have help and support.
Ex: The teacher provides a student with a visual aid, such as a picture card or a communication board, to help them share their thoughts during a class discussion about a familiar topic.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Ask questions related to information in a discussion.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can ask questions to get more information or clarify my understanding during a discussion.
Ex: During a class discussion about a field trip to the zoo, a student asks, "What kind of animals did we see in the reptile house?" or "Can you explain what a mammal is again?"
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can share my thoughts and ideas directly with my classmates during a discussion, and respond to what they say.
Ex: In a small group, a student responds to a classmate's comment about a story by saying, "That's funny! I liked that part too," or "That reminds me of a time when..."
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate in discussions with my classmates by listening and responding to others.
Ex: During a circle time discussion, a student uses a nonverbal cue, such as a thumbs up or a head nod, to indicate their agreement or understanding. They might also point to a picture or object related to the discussion topic.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can participate in a discussion by making relevant comments and connecting my ideas to what others are saying.
Ex: During a group discussion about a story, a student comments on a character's actions and adds, "That's just like what [classmate's name] said about the character being brave!"
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can answer questions about the main points of a discussion.
Ex: When a teacher asks, "What was the main problem in the story we just read?" the student can briefly explain the central conflict.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can answer simple questions about who or what is being discussed.
Ex: When asked, "Who is the main character in this story?" the student can correctly identify the character by name.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify the explicitly stated main idea of a text presented orally or through other media.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the main idea of a text presented in different ways, like read aloud or in a video.
Ex: After watching a short video about the water cycle, the student can accurately state the main idea: "The water cycle shows how water moves from the earth to the sky and back again."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify the main idea of a text when it is presented in different ways with support.
Ex: The teacher provides a graphic organizer with visual cues to help students identify the main idea of a news segment about a local community event.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can pick out details from a text presented in different ways with support.
Ex: After listening to a story, the teacher asks the student to point to a picture that shows the main event of the story.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Identify the reasons and evidence supporting a specific point that the speaker makes.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify the main point a speaker is making and some of the reasons or evidence they use to support it.
Ex: After listening to a teacher explain why it is important to wear a helmet while biking, a student can state the main point (helmets prevent injuries) and recall one reason (helmets protect your head).
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify a point that a speaker makes.
Ex: After listening to a classmate share their opinion about a book, a student can repeat one thing the classmate liked or disliked about the book.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize who is speaking.
Ex: When asked, "Who is telling us about the weather today?" a student can correctly identify the news reporter on the television screen.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Clearly report on a familiar topic or text or present an opinion including related facts.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can create a simple presentation about a topic we are learning about in class and share my opinion about it. 
Ex: After learning about different animal habitats, a student creates a simple one page presentation about the rainforest. They share their opinion about why they think it's an important habitat and include facts about the animals and plants that live there.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use my words or pictures to share information about a topic I know well.
Ex: A student chooses to share about their favorite animal. They might tell the class its name and what it likes to eat or show a picture of it.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate in a presentation with my classmates.
Ex: During a class presentation, a student can help hold up pictures, point to parts of a poster when asked, or answer a simple question about the topic.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Select or create audio recordings and visual/tactile displays to enhance a presentation.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can choose or create audio recordings, pictures, or objects to make my presentation more interesting and easier to understand but may not be linked to the main idea. 
Ex: For a presentation about different types of weather, a student might choose pictures of each weather type and play a sound recording of rain for the "rainy" slide.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can choose from different audio recordings, pictures, or objects to add to a presentation with support .
Ex: After the teacher narrows down the options, a student can choose the best picture to represent the main character in a story from a set of three.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can collaborate with my classmates to choose audio recordings, pictures, or objects for our group presentation.
Ex: While working on a group presentation about the ocean, a student can point to their favorite sea creature picture from a collection to include on the poster.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can with guidance and support, compose simple writing for different purposes, using basic sentences and vocabulary. 
I may use pictures and symbols to support writing. Can participate in the revision process with support.
Example (Low-Stakes): (Student draws a picture of a cat) "This is my cat, Mittens. She is soft and likes to play with string."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can with support, express an opinion about a topic or text and provide a simple reason to support that opinion. 
I may use pictures and symbols to enhance writing.
Example (Opinion): (Teacher: "What did you think of the story?") Student: "I liked the story. The dog was funny." (Student draws a picture of a dog with its tongue out.)
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with significant support, introduce a topic or text and state a simple opinion about it.
I may use pictures and symbols as the primary form of communication.
Example (Topic Introduction): (Teacher shows a picture of a lion) "This is a lion. Do you like lions?" Student: "Yes!"

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, use writing, dictation and/or drawing to compose: a. Opinion pieces in which they clearly state an opinion about a topic or text and include some reasons to support that opinion.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
Composes simple opinion pieces, clearly stating an opinion and providing a few reasons with some detail, using pictures, symbols, or dictation to support writing.
Example: (Student draws a picture of children playing on a sunny playground.) "I like to play outside. The sun feels good, and I can run around."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
With prompting and support, can state an opinion about a topic or text and provide a simple reason to justify that opinion, possibly using pictures and symbols to enhance communication.
Example: (Teacher: "Where do you like to play - inside or outside?") Student: "Outside! It's more fun." (Student draws a smiley face next to the word "outside.")
descriptors.cc_emerging:
With significant support, can express a preference or opinion about a topic, possibly relying primarily on nonverbal communication or single words to convey their stance.
Example: (Teacher points to a picture of a playground and a picture of a living room.) "Which one do you like better?" Student points to the picture of the playground.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Informative/Explanatory text in which they introduce a topic and provide some facts, details, and/or multimedia content about a predetermined or self chosen topic.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write or dictate informative texts that introduce a topic clearly and provide some supporting facts, details, and/or multimedia elements.
Ex: A student chooses to write about their favorite animal, a dog. They write a paragraph describing dogs, including details about their care, and draw a picture of a dog.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
With prompting and support, I can contribute facts, details, or other information related to a topic, possibly using pictures and symbols to support communication.
Ex: In a small group led by the teacher, a student contributes information about a cat ("Cats meow. They like to sleep.") when prompted and draws a picture of a cat on a shared piece of chart paper.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can express interest in a topic and, with significant support, contribute simple information or preferences.
Ex: When shown a picture of a rainforest, a student points excitedly to a monkey and vocalizes, prompting the teacher to write "monkey" on a graphic organizer.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Convey events, real or imagined and narrate a single event or several loosely linked events. Include some details regarding what happened and tell about the events in the order in which they occurred.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can with support, retell or describe events or experiences in a sequential order, using simple words, phrases, and/or pictures.
Ex: Using a visual schedule, a student retells the steps they took to make a craft project, using short phrases and pointing to corresponding pictures.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can contribute ideas to a story with support, retelling familiar stories or experiences using simple words and possibly drawings.
Ex: In a shared writing activity, the teacher writes a story about a hidden door based on student input. Students contribute ideas for what might be behind the door, and one student draws a picture to accompany the class story.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate in shared storytelling experiences, contributing a word, phrase, or action related to a familiar event or routine.
Ex: During circle time, the teacher leads a retelling of the morning routine. When prompted, a student makes a gesture to show washing hands, one of the steps in the routine.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that includes an introduction, body, and conclusion. uses familiar words, transitions to link and build connections, and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can create a text with a beginning and ending using words, pictures, and/or dictation. I can use some transition words to connect my ideas and show the order of events.
Ex: A student creates a book about their dream vacation. They draw pictures for each page, dictate a sentence or two about what is happening, and use transition words like "first," "next," and "finally" to show the sequence of events.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
With support, I can create a text that tells about an event or experience. I can use words, pictures, and/or dictation to share my ideas and show the order in which things happened.
Ex: A student works with a partner to create a comic strip about a time they helped someone. They take turns drawing pictures in the frames, and the teacher helps them add words and speech bubbles to tell the story.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can communicate about an event or experience using a combination of drawing, dictation, gestures, and/or single words.

subject: ELA
text: Produce writing that is appropriate for an explicitly stated task or purpose, and expresses more than one idea.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write to communicate more than one idea for a specific purpose. My writing is understandable.
Ex: A student is asked to write about their favorite thing to do outside. They dictate three sentences, each describing a different activity they enjoy.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
With support, I can write or dictate to communicate an idea or preference for a specific purpose.
Ex: A student is asked to write about their favorite animal. With prompting from the teacher, they dictate a sentence about their favorite animal and draw a picture.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can communicate a preference or choice through pointing, gesturing, or using a single word or symbol.
Ex: When asked to choose between two writing prompts (one about animals, one about vehicles), a student points to the picture that represents their preferred topic.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support from adults and peers, plan before writing and produce writing focused on the planned topic, and revise their own writing, dictation, or pictures.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can plan my writing before I start, stay focused on my topic, and make changes to improve my work.
Ex: A student uses a story map to plan out the beginning, middle, and end of their narrative before they begin writing or dictating their story.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
With help, I can plan my writing by sharing my ideas and add to my writing to make it better.
Ex: A student, working with a partner, brainstorms ideas for a class report about weather. After drafting, they add a sentence with more information about their favorite type of weather.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can communicate my ideas and make choices about my writing with support.
Ex: A student chooses a picture from a selection provided by the teacher to represent the main idea of their writing piece.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support from adults, use digital tools, including the Internet, to produce writing while interacting and collaborating with others. Learn to produce writing through printing, cursive, and/or typing.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use digital tools to write and share my work with others, with help from adults. I am learning to write using different methods like printing, cursive, or typing.
Ex: A student uses a word processing program to write a paragraph about their favorite book, then shares their writing with a classmate for feedback.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
With help, I can use technology to write and work with others on writing projects.
Ex: A student dictates a sentence about a picture to an adult, who types it into a shared document. They then take turns adding sentences with their partner.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use technology to communicate with help from an adult.
Ex: A student uses a picture-based communication app to select images that represent their ideas for a story. An adult helps them to share these ideas with the class.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support, identify information about two or more aspects of a shared or independent inquiry topic.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can explore a research topic with help and find information from different sources. I can share what I learn with others.
Ex: Students are working on a project about their community. With help from the teacher, they identify key places in their community and then use photographs and interviews with community members to gather information.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
With help, I can learn about a topic by using different sources to find information.
Ex: A teacher reads aloud two different accounts of the same historical event. Students then work with a partner to identify key details from each source and discuss any differences they notice.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate in a group research project to learn about a topic.
Ex: Students are working in small groups to research different animals. Each student is assigned a specific role in the research process (e.g., finding pictures, writing down facts). The group then shares their findings with the class.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print or digital sources, sort information into given categories, and write or draw about each one.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use information from my own experiences and from things I read or view to help me write. I can organize information into different groups.
Ex: Students are writing a report about different types of animals. They use a graphic organizer to sort information they have gathered from books and websites into categories like "mammals," "reptiles," and "birds."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use my own experiences to help me write.
Ex: Students are writing a personal narrative about a time they overcame a challenge. They use a story map to recall and sequence the key events and emotions they experienced.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can share my experiences with others by speaking and drawing.
Ex: Students are discussing a class field trip. With prompting from the teacher, they share details about what they saw and did during the trip.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: With guidance and support from adults, recall key details from literary or informational texts to support reflection or inquiry questions based on a reading of a literary or informational text.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify important details in stories and informational texts. I can use these details to answer questions and think more deeply about what I read.
Ex: After reading a nonfiction article about animal adaptations, students work in small groups to answer questions about the text. They use evidence from the text to support their answers.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use what I am learning in reading to understand different types of stories and information.
Ex: After listening to a folktale, a teacher helps students compare and contrast the main characters using a Venn Diagram. Students then use their observations to discuss the lesson or moral of the story.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate in conversations and activities about the stories and information we read together in class.
Ex: After a shared reading of a poem, students participate in a group activity where they draw pictures to represent key images or themes from the poem.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

I can given a topic and a sample brainstorming bubble, generate ideas and write them down, then reread what is written and add one more detail.
I can Using a question framework (e.g., 5 W’s and an H) in graphic organizer software, take turns entering information into the organizer, seek another peer partner group’s feedback, and then add to the outline.
I can after reading a science text, work with a classmate to take notes in graphic organizer software, convert the graphic representation into an outline, and use word prediction software with a specific topic dictionary to complete the L column of a KWL chart, share it with another pair of classmates, and revise based on their feedback.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, develop writing by planning and revising own writing by adding more information.
I can after sharing writing with peers, work with peers to brainstorm ideas to add. Peers write all of the ideas in a list and give it to the student to use in revising and adding more information to improve the overall quality of the writing.
I can Work with peers to plan a written report of their research project. Each takes turns reading what they have to one another and then the group works together to add ideas to a graphic organizer provided by the teacher. Finally, the student adds ideas from the graphic organizer to own writing to strengthen it.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, add more to writing to clarify message.
I can When asked by an adult or peer to add more, select additional letters or words to add to the overall message.
I can with teacher guidance and support and using word prediction software (e.g., The teacher asks, “What sound do you hear at the beginning of cat?”), and a talking word processor (e.g., The teacher says, “It said car. I thought you were trying to write cat. What can we change to make it say cat?”), label familiar pictures from a favorite text.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: make intentional decisions about technology use (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, and/or other interactive formats) to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products. Proficiently produce writing through printing, cursive, and/or typing.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products.
I can use technology to add a sentence in an electronic shared writing product.
I can add words to sentences in an electronic shared writing product.
I can use online communication software to text message with an e-buddy in another classroom or school.
I can record daily activities on a blog that is shared with parents instead of a traditional home-school notebook.
I can navigate the Internet using screen reader software, identify information about the selected topic, use the information to write using a talking word processor with an alternative keyboard, and share what was learned with classmates.
I can use a teacher-created or teacher-identified website to learn about a topic with a peer, take notes with the peer in graphic organizer software, convert the graphic organizer to an outline, and co-author a summary.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update shared writing products.
I can after reviewing and discussing a shared writing product, add words to sentences in the electronic shared writing product.
I can having sent an e-mail to an adult, read their response seeking additional information or clarification, and write a new e-mail to address the request.
I can use an alternative keyboard programmed with the day’s activities and some comments to write an entry on a blog that is shared with parents instead of a home-school notebook.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use technology to write.
I can use a keyboard to type letters and words interactively with a peer or an adult who types simple, conventionally spelled messages.
I can use a keyboard programmed for only alphabet letters and a space bar, word prediction software, and a talking word processor with a peer model to take turns typing text messages to one another.

source: Wisconsin Essential Elements (DPI), linked from WI-CC-ELA

subject: ELA
text: with guidance and support as needed, conduct inquiry projects to answer a question or solve a problem.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can conduct inquiry projects to answer a question or solve a problem with guidance and support as needed.
I can Investigate a question or problem by gathering information from various sources and presenting my findings with assistance.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can conduct simple inquiry projects with guidance to answer questions or solve problems.
I can with help, research a basic question or problem and share what I learned.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance, participate in simple inquiry activities to answer questions or solve problems.
I can with support, explore a simple question or problem and communicate my findings.

subject: ELA
text: write answers to research questions by selecting relevant information from multiple resources.

descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can select information from multiple sources and use the information to write answers to research questions.
I can given a topic, a collection of bookmarked websites, and a set of guiding questions, use a screen reader to read the sites and select information about the topic. Then, use the information to answer questions.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select information from multiple sources and use the information to write answers to research questions.
I can given a topic, a collection of bookmarked websites, and a set of guiding questions, navigate to each site and copy/paste information to answer the questions.
I can given a topic, a collection of bookmarked websites, and a set of guiding questions, navigate to each site, listen and read the information with a screen reader, and use word prediction software with a talking word processor to write their answers.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use information from one source to answer a question.
I can given a guiding question, use a single message voice output communication device to say, “That’s it” when the teacher reads something from a teacher-selected text that answers the question.
I can with teacher guidance and support as needed with any of the steps: given a topic, a single bookmarked website, a what or where question, use a screen reader to listen to and read the information at the site, and use word prediction software with a talking word processor and adapted keyboard presenting only alphabet letters, space bar, and a period, write an answer.

text: with guidance and support from adults, draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support reflection, analysis or inquiry questions based on a reading of a literary or informational text.

I can find some evidence in texts to support my thoughts with guidance.
I can Identify and use basic quotes or details from a text to support my ideas with help.

I can with support, find and use simple details from a text to back up my thoughts.
